title: PetOverlay follow + single-frame sprite rendering + single-pet favicon/app icon

requirements.summary: Make PetOverlay smoothly follow user pointer during active sessions while staying non-blocking and clamped to the viewport.
acceptanceCriteria: During an active focus/break session, the pet overlay repositions in response to pointer movement (smoothly, without jitter).
The overlay never blocks clicks/typing in underlying UI except for its own controls (e.g., mute button remains clickable).
The overlay clamps to the viewport so it cannot drift off-screen.

file_operations.description: Add a reusable hook that subscribes to pointer movement, computes a smoothed target position (e.g., via requestAnimationFrame interpolation), and returns a clamped (x,y) position that keeps the overlay fully on-screen.

Replace the fixed bottom-right positioning with transform-based positioning driven by the pointer-follow hook; keep the outer container pointer-events-none and ensure only the pet controls (mute button / bubble if interactive) use pointer-events-auto; clamp overlay bounds using the hook to prevent drifting off-screen.

requirements.summary: Render only a single 128x128 sprite frame in PetOverlay and keep bubble/mute positioning aligned to that frame.
acceptanceCriteria: The PetOverlay displays exactly one 128x128 sprite frame (no adjacent frames from the sprite sheet are visible).
Changing mood/phase swaps the visible frame correctly without resizing or showing multiple pets.
The layout matches the intent shown in the uploaded screenshot (single pet body with bubble above; no multi-frame strip visible).

file_operations.description: Adjust sprite metadata returned by getPetSprite to support true single-frame cropping (e.g., return background positioning/sizing information suitable for a 128x128 viewport) so adjacent frames cannot appear.

Update sprite rendering to ensure only one 128x128 frame is visible (e.g., render within a 128x128 overflow-hidden viewport or use a background-image approach); verify the speech bubble anchor and mute icon remain positioned relative to the single visible frame.

requirements.summary: Update favicon/app icon to a single-pet pixel-art icon and wire it into HTML and any manifest configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Browser tab icon renders as a single pet icon (not a sprite strip / multiple pets).
If a web manifest is present/used by the build, it references the new single-pet icon asset(s) and no longer points to sprite sheets.
No console errors related to missing icon assets.

file_operations.description: Add the generated pixel-art single-pet (cat) app icon asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/app-icon-cat.dim_512x512.png.
Add the generated pixel-art single-pet (dog) app icon asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/app-icon-dog.dim_512x512.png.
Add the generated pixel-art single-pet (cat) favicon asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon-cat.dim_64x64.png.
Add the generated pixel-art single-pet (dog) favicon asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon-dog.dim_64x64.png.

Wire the favicon to the new single-pet asset (use frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon-cat.dim_64x64.png as the default) and include manifest linkage if present/added; ensure no references to sprite sheets are used for tab icons.

Add a web manifest referencing the new single-pet app icon assets (use frontend/public/assets/generated/app-icon-cat.dim_512x512.png as the default, optionally include the dog variant as an additional icon entry) so PWA/icon configuration does not point to sprite sheets.
